commits.summary: Set up toolchain, approaches doc, and LLM trace capture
commits.body:
- setup/ubuntu-wsl: installer + doctor for Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2), amd64/arm64
- docs/approaches.md: bytecode- and native-level verification plan
- infra/langfuse: pinned local Langfuse stack
- tools/traces: publish redacted Claude Code traces, link them to jj changes

History note: rewritten on 2026-10-24, before anyone had cloned the repo, to the
per-session trace layout of docs/traces.md. The LLM-Trace line below was added then.

commits.summary: Restructure traces: per-session manifest + content-addressed logs
commits.body:
- traces/<session-id>/manifest.json (checked in): stats, context windows,
  tools, files touched, log pointer, commits
- traces/<session-id>/logs/<sha256>.jsonl.gz (gitignored): immutable,
  append-only redacted log snapshots named by the sha256 of their content
- commits carry 'LLM-Trace: <session-id> sha256:<log-sha256>'; the
  manifest lists them by jj change id (+ git SHA once immutable)
- jj trace-commit / trace-push aliases; check verifies hashes, trailers,
  redaction and that each commit's in-tree manifest names its trailer log

commits.summary: Publish trace logs on Cloudflare at terminalvalue.net/raw-traces
commits.body:
- infra/cdn: read-only Worker serving R2 bucket llm-traces on the
  route terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/* (edge-cached, immutable)
- sync.py upload: put commit-referenced logs in R2, re-download through
  the CDN and verify sha256 before recording the URL
- trace-push uploads before pushing; check --remote re-verifies uploads
- installer: Linux Node 24 for the pinned wrangler

commits.summary: Harden traces before launch: redaction policy 3, logs table, licenses
commits.body:
Pre-launch review of what cannot change once the repo has been cloned:
- redaction policy 3: emails match case-insensitively, GitHub noreply
  addresses are kept, organizationUuid/accountUuid are scrubbed, and
  thinking-block signatures are dropped
- manifest: structured `client`, one `logs` table (sizes + URL) instead
  of uploads/locations/log_url, no local-only langfuse block
- trace-commit describes before it syncs, so the manifest frozen in a
  commit lists that commit under its real summary
- a session stamps the changes created while it ran, plus @ when it is
  the running session (author_date window instead of open-ended)
- LICENSE (Apache-2.0) for code, LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0 for docs/ and traces/
- the first three commits were rewritten to this layout; see the
  history note in docs/traces.md

commits.summary: Publish sessions under changes/ with summaries, an index and agent procedure
commits.body:
Traces move from traces/ to changes/traces/. Each session now gets a summary.md rendered from changes/summary-template.md: the commits it made with their full messages, then every prompt with the final reply, all derived from the redacted log. changes/index.json is a small global manifest listing every session and its commits; the detailed metadata stays per session. Commit messages gain two link trailers, LLM-Trace-Summary and LLM-Trace-Log, above the LLM-Trace identifier.

changes/README.md and CLAUDE.md give agents the procedure: commit each finished feature with sync.py commit (repeatable -m paragraphs) without asking, run check, and push only when asked. .claude/settings.json allows exactly those commands. Also adds sync.py unpublish, which deletes a log from R2 and purges it from the Cloudflare cache with a dedicated API token.

Verified: check reports 0 errors; the trailer helpers were tested with an existing Co-Authored-By block, re-stamping and a second session; git interpret-trailers parses the block; the Stop hook runs cleanly.

commits.summary: Link the full trace prominently at the top of each summary
commits.body: summary.md now opens with a download link to the session's log on the CDN, with its size and short sha256, instead of only listing it in the metadata table.

commits.summary: Update session trace through the push and repo description
commits.body: Generated trace files only: the manifest, summary and index now cover the turns after the last push.

commits.summary: Add Box Office, a distributed ticketing system to verify
commits.body:
apps/boxoffice is a Gradle multi-module build (Java 25, Spring Boot 4.1.1) with two services, ticketing and payments, that share nothing but Kafka topics. Ticketing exposes synchronous capabilities (create a concert, see availability, hold seats under a lease with all-or-nothing semantics) and asynchronous ones (place and cancel orders, answered 202 and settled by a saga with the payment service). Each service owns a MongoDB database and uses a transactional outbox, an idempotent inbox, conditional updates, transaction retry and dead-letter topics. A late payment for an expired hold, and a cancellation, are compensated by a refund.

The order state machine and seat rules are pure Java in ticketing-domain, as the first target for verification tools. The README states the safety and liveness invariants the verification scenarios should establish, and lists known gaps (relay without a lease, clock skew, gateway call inside a transaction) as scenarios for tools to find.

Verified with ./gradlew build: 29 tests pass. They include a bounded model check of every order input sequence up to six inputs, a component test of duplicated and reordered payment commands, and 8 end-to-end tests against Kafka and a MongoDB replica set in Testcontainers (happy path, decline, cancel and refund, a late capture after the hold expired, 16 concurrent holds on one seat with exactly one winner, idempotent retries). Each end-to-end test checks the cross-service invariants against both databases. The compose.yaml and curl walkthrough in the README were also run by hand.

commits.summary: Add behavioural contracts: a CI gate that proves behaviour unchanged
commits.body:
tools/contracts is a dependency-free verifier (Java 25, ClassFile API). For a method it derives a contract, the outcome of every possible input, which is checked in next to the code. The build fails when the bytecode no longer matches it, and an intended change shows up as a reviewable diff of exactly the cases that changed. The contract is a proof, not a sample: purity is proved from bytecode (a closed-world walk through sealed hierarchies, with a short list of trusted JDK APIs), the input domain is derived from enums, booleans, records and sealed types, and every input is executed. Methods that are impure or have unbounded inputs are refused. A Gradle convention plugin adds verifyContracts to check and updateContracts, and writes SARIF for GitHub code scanning and SonarQube. Box Office's OrderLifecycle#decide is the first target: 36 cases.

Why this approach: JBMC 6.11 was tried first and cannot handle modern Java as it ships. It treats the pattern-switch typeSwitch invokedynamic as an unknown value, and has no models for List.of, record equals or Math.multiplyExact; docs/approaches.md records this as B5's finding and the POC as B8. Verified with 7 unit tests of the verifier (pure, static write, clock read, open interface, unbounded domain, diff, update then drift) and by trying three changes on the real code: a case-merging cleanup that kept money for declined orders (caught, 2 cases), a refactor from switch to == that the agent believed equivalent but which changed null handling (caught, 1 case), and an Instant.now() call (refused as impure). A genuinely equivalent refactor passes. ./gradlew build passes with verifyContracts in check.

commits.summary: Add numbered, generated formal verification examples
commits.body:
examples/ is now the entry point of the repo: five numbered examples of code changes run through the behavioural-contract verifier, with a table of contents. Each example is a folder with two authored files, example.json (the change, its risk, the expected verdict and the explanation, in the format of examples/schema/example.schema.json) and change.patch. tools/examples/build.py applies each patch to a temporary copy of the repo, runs the module's unit tests and the verifier, and writes what they produced: result.json (verdict, counterexamples, before and after excerpts, the contract diff for intended changes, the unit-test outcome; examples/schema/result.schema.json), result.sarif, the console output, and a README page. It then regenerates the table of contents and examples/index.json. Nothing in a page is claimed by hand, and the generator fails if a verdict differs from the expected one, so the examples are also regression tests of the verifier.

The examples are a case-merging cleanup that keeps money for declined orders (violation; the repo's own model-checking test also catches it), a refactor from switch to == that the agent believed equivalent (violation; all unit tests pass), a timestamp in the decision (unverifiable; tests pass), an equivalent refactor (verified), and an intended message change reviewed as a one-line contract diff (verified). Measuring the unit tests corrected a claim in the first draft of example 001, which said the tests pass. The verifier now prints its proof statistics on failure too, and gives advice that fits an unverifiable method. Verified: all five verdicts match their expectations, both schemas validate the files, two consecutive runs produce identical output, and the verifier's tests and ticketing-domain check pass.

commits.summary: Split the repo into examples/ and llm-dlc/
commits.body:
The repo is reorganised by concern so it is easier to browse. examples/ now holds everything about formal verification: the numbered examples, approaches.md, apps/boxoffice, the contracts verifier (tools/contracts), the generator (tools/build.py) and the toolchain setup, whose instructions moved from the root README to setup/README.md. llm-dlc/ is the meta example: the procedure and session index (the old changes/README.md), specification.md (the old docs/traces.md), the traces, sync.py and the CDN and Langfuse infrastructure. The root README is now a short landing page for the two.

sync.py, the Stop and SessionEnd hooks, the permissions, the jj aliases, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore and every relative link follow the move. check also looks for manifests under changes/traces in older commits. Log IDs and CDN URLs are unchanged, but the LLM-Trace-Summary links of earlier commits still name changes/traces on main, which no longer exists; the specification records this.

Verified from the new paths: 7 verifier tests; 29 Box Office tests, with the 8 end-to-end tests rerun without the build cache; all 5 examples regenerated with their expected verdicts; 60 Markdown links resolved, apart from one template placeholder; sync.py sync and check report 0 errors.
